body:
This is arguably a reduction in performance as it turns one `get_extension().to_lower()` into two, I'd not replace this case if the goal is performance (I think both have equivalent readability)

Also typo:
```suggestion
	if (!p_path.has_extension("tscn") && !p_path.has_extension("tres")) {
```
Same here with replacing one check with two, I'd leave it as is
I'd leave these separately, they're unrelated and does nominally change behavior, so would be better to not bundle them with a new feature
`has_extension()` does not perform `get_extension().to_lower()` directly, but yeah, I didn't check which one is faster (might be the new one).
Not so much which is faster but doing the case insensitive part twice instead of casting once and then doing plain comparison

This doesn't work, `get_data` returns `char32_t`, so the other method would have to be `bool has_extension(const char32_t *p_ext) const;`

But it should really call with `String` no reason to have it callable with `char32_t` (especially since that will cause overload issues)

Is it safe to cast it to `char *`? 🤔
I wanted to avoid duplicate code, but also provide a char overload, so Strings are not constructed unnecessarily.
No it wouldnt work, the `char *` overload takes Latin1 strings, not utf32, even if we restrict the suffices to latin1 it won't work with casting `char32_t *`
Well, I'll just remove the String overload, because right now it's not used anyway.
Burt regardless it won't constuct strings unnecessarily for literals, `p_path.has_extension("foo")` will call the `const char *` version
It is used in several places

Aren't these two branches the same as `_find_upper(*this_str) != _find_upper(*p_ext)`?

Same in the other overload.
Indeed the comparison is only needed for `nocasecmp` etc.
This was not removed along with other cases like it, was that intentional? I think all should be separated out to remove any behavioral differences
